newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada help wanted index rises 1.0 pct in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Canada help wanted index rises 1.0 pct in Oct.

text.p: Canada's help wanted index, seasonally adjusted, rose 1.0 percent in October to 88 (1991=100) from 87 in September, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
The Ontario index rose two percent to 93 while the Quebec index declined one percent to 95, the federal government agency reported.

The help wanted index monitors changes in help wanted advertisements in 20 cities. It reflects the intent of employers in these labor markets to hire new workers. Increases in the index are usually followed by drops in the unemployment rate.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a rise in the index to 87.8 points.
(For more information on this release from Statistics Canada's Labour Division, contact Michael Scrim at 613-951-4090.)
